summary: Menu text word-wrap measurer. Fetches the text string through **(this+0xE0) (falling back to byte_5EA438), binary-searches with a step starting at 32 for the largest offset from a2 whose a2-prefixed substring still fits the width constraint this+0x100, measuring each candidate with TextRenderToSurface after temporarily nulling the probe character and (when this+0xC8 exists) routing the resource path through sub_498560(*(*(this+0xC8)+0x40)). When the found position is non-null it backtracks to the nearest word boundary (space 0x20 or 0xFF), then scans forward to return the final wrap offset. Called by the four menu layout/cursor helpers.

local_names.a2: start offset into the text string for measuring and wrapping
local_names.v3: text string fetched from **(this+0xE0), falling back to byte_5EA438
local_names.v4: string length plus the terminating character (strlen(v3) + 1)
local_names.v15: probe character saved and restored around the width measurement
local_names.v17: measured text width returned by TextRenderToSurface

operations.description: v3 = **(this + 0xE0) fetches the text string pointer; if null, fall back to the global default byte_5EA438.
v4 = strlen(v3) + 1 computes the string length including the terminator.

Binary search with step v6 (starting at 32) for the largest offset v5 from a2 whose substring fits: probe v7 = v6 + v5 while v7 <= v4 - 1; on a failing probe halve the step (v6 /= 2); continue while v6 > 0.
If the object at this+0xC8 exists, sub_498560(*(*(this + 0xC8) + 0x40)) processes the resource path; a null path falls back to byte_5EA438.
TextRenderToSurface(&v3[a2], &v17, v18, 1) measures the rendered width of the a2-prefixed substring into v17, with the probe character v15 temporarily nulled and restored.
If the measured width v17 <= this+0x100, accept the candidate (v16 = v7); otherwise halve the step (v6 /= 2).
If the character at the found offset v5 is non-null, backtrack from v5-1 toward a2 to the nearest word boundary (space 0x20 or 0xFF) and advance one character past it.
Scan forward from a2 to v5, stopping before the first 0xFF terminator, and return the final wrap offset. Used by the four menu layout/cursor helpers.
